# `Codec`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Codec — one invariant codec that drives BOTH the JSON direction and the
DB column shape.

A `Codec a` bundles an encoder, a decoder, and a structural `Shape` for one
type in a single value, so the wire form and the storage form cannot drift
apart: you cannot hold a codec that encodes but does not decode, nor one whose
column list disagrees with its fields. This is bidirectionality AND
schema-agreement enforced by the type, not by discipline. `toJson codec` and
`fromJson codec` read the same codec, so the round-trip law
`fromJson codec (toJson codec x) == Ok x` holds by construction, and `shape
codec` reads the SAME codec, so the DB column set is derived from the same
fact the JSON round-trip uses.

`map` is the load-bearing scalar combinator and is a BIJECTION — it takes BOTH
directions (`a -> b` and `b -> a`). A one-way map could not encode a `b`,
because the encoder needs `b -> a` to reach the underlying encoder. Requiring
the inverse makes the drift a covariant map would permit impossible to write.

Representation note (why the decoder is stored as a factory, not a bare
`Decoder a`): the runtime JSON `Decoder` is a single-shot carrier — running it
consumes it — so a codec that must be reused across encode/decode calls cannot
hold one `Decoder a` value directly. `Codec a` stores the decode side as
`{} -> Decoder a`: a reproducible factory that builds a fresh decoder on each
run. Both function fields are stored on a shared, clonable carrier, so a
`Codec a` is an ordinary reusable value that composes.

The `Shape` field. Every codec carries a `Shape` describing how it maps to DB
columns, in dialect-neutral `ColType`s (the `Ipe.Db` layer chooses the actual
SQLite/Postgres types). A bare scalar is one typed column (`SScalar`); a
record built with the field builder is a list of typed columns (`SRecord`); a
nested record, list, dict, or data-carrying union is one JSON-in-TEXT column
(`SBlob`). One codec therefore supplies the column list, the reads, and the
writes from a single source.

Building composite codecs: `list`/`maybe`/`dict` lift an element codec over a
container by lifting each side (the encoder over the container, the decoder
factory through the matching JSON kernel), and each derives its own `Shape`.

A record codec is written as one `Codec` value directly: the encoder is an
`Ipe.Json.Encode.object` over the field encoders, the decoder factory is a
`Decode.succeed <constructor> |> Pipeline.required <key> <fieldDecoder> …`
applicative chain over the field decoders, and the `shp` field is the
record's `SRecord` column list — each field named once per side, and its
column type read from the field codec's own `Shape`. This form is fully
monomorphic: the constructor and the pipeline decoder are concrete at the
record's own definition site, so they lower directly.

The combinator surface:

  * `string` / `int` / `bool` / `float` — the scalar codecs.
  * `decimal` / `money` — exact-decimal scalars encoded LOSSLESSLY as a JSON
    string (never a `Float`), for prices and quantities a `Float` would
    corrupt. `decimal` maps to `CDecimal` (binds as `SqlDecimal`); `money`
    maps to `CMoney` (binds as `SqlMoney`) — the role is in the tag, never
    collapsed to a bare `SqlString`.
  * `map toB toA inner` — a bijection newtype wrapper (a `Codec a` to a
    `Codec b` given both directions).
  * `list elem` — a JSON array of `elem`s ⇄ `List a`.
  * `maybe elem` — JSON `null` ⇄ `Nothing`, any other value ⇄ `Just`.
  * `dict value` — a JSON object of `value`s ⇄ `Dict String a`.
  * `enum eq pairs` — a nullary enum ⇄ a readable JSON string, driven by one
    `(constructor, wireName)` association list; fail-closed on an unknown tag.
  * `taggedUnion variants` with `var0`/`var1`/`var2`/`var3` — a data-carrying
    ADT ⇄ a tagged JSON array `["Tag", arg0, …]`; each `Variant` carries both
    directions, so the union is one source of truth.
  * `shape` — the codec's `Shape`: the derived DB column list / scalar type.
  * `toValue` / `toJson` / `fromJson` — encode to a JSON `Value` / string,
    decode a JSON string back (a typed `Err` on malformed input, never a
    panic).
  * `fromJsonSafe maxChars` — decode, rejecting input over `maxChars` BEFORE
    parsing (the untrusted-input door).

Minimal round-trips:

    import Ipe.Codec as Codec exposing (Codec)

    scores : Codec (Dict String Int)
    scores =
        Codec.dict Codec.int

    -- Codec.fromJson scores (Codec.toJson scores d) == Ok d

    type Rank = Bronze | Silver | Gold

    rankCodec : Codec Rank
    rankCodec =
        Codec.enum rankEq
            [ ( Bronze, "bronze" ), ( Silver, "silver" ), ( Gold, "gold" ) ]

    -- Codec.fromJson rankCodec (Codec.toJson rankCodec Gold) == Ok Gold
    -- Codec.fromJson rankCodec "\"platinum\"" == Err … (unknown tag)

    type alias User =
        { id : String, age : Int, active : Bool }

    makeUser : String -> Int -> Bool -> User
    makeUser id age active =
        { id = id, age = age, active = active }

    userCodec : Codec User
    userCodec =
        Codec
            { enc =
                \u ->
                    Encode.object
                        [ ( "id", Codec.toValue Codec.string u.id )
                        , ( "age", Codec.toValue Codec.int u.age )
                        , ( "active", Codec.toValue Codec.bool u.active )
                        ]
            , mkDec =
                \_ ->
                    Decode.succeed makeUser
                        |> Pipeline.required "id" Decode.string
                        |> Pipeline.required "age" Decode.int
                        |> Pipeline.required "active" Decode.bool
            , shp =
                SRecord [ ( "id", CText ), ( "age", CInt ), ( "active", CBool ) ]
            }

    -- Codec.fromJson userCodec (Codec.toJson userCodec u) == Ok u
    -- Codec.shape userCodec
    --     == SRecord [ ( "id", CText ), ( "age", CInt ), ( "active", CBool ) ]

## `Codec`

An invariant codec for `a`: an encoder to a JSON `Value`, a decoder factory
that builds a fresh decoder for `a`, and the structural `Shape` its DB columns
derive from. Invariant in `a` — it both produces and consumes `a`, which is
what keeps the two directions in step; the `Shape` keeps the storage form in
step with them.

## `ColType`

The dialect-neutral column type a codec maps to. The `Ipe.Db` layer maps
these to concrete SQLite/Postgres types (`TEXT`/`VARCHAR`, `INTEGER`/`BOOLEAN`,
…), so one codec works on every backend. `CNull t` is a nullable column of `t`.
`CTime` is an instant stored as Unix milliseconds — INTEGER affinity like
`CInt`, but it binds as the `SqlTime` role so a moment in time is never
confused with a plain count. `CDecimal` stores an exact decimal as a lossless
TEXT string and binds as `SqlDecimal`; `CMoney` stores an "AMOUNT ISO_CODE"
TEXT string and binds as `SqlMoney` — neither is ever coerced through a lossy
`Float` or confused with a bare `SqlString`.

## `Shape`

A codec's structural shape. `SRecord` is a record whose top-level scalar
fields become typed columns; `SScalar` is one bare scalar codec as a single
typed column; `SBlob` is a nested record / list / dict / data-carrying ADT
stored as one JSON TEXT column.

## `shape`

```ipe
shape : Codec a -> Shape
```

The codec's structural `Shape` — its DB column list (`SRecord`), single
scalar column type (`SScalar`), or one JSON-TEXT blob column (`SBlob`).

    shape (Codec.list Codec.int) == SBlob
    shape Codec.int == SScalar CInt
    shape (Codec.maybe Codec.string) == SScalar (CNull CText)

## `columnOf`

```ipe
columnOf : Shape -> ColType
```

The column type a record FIELD contributes to an `SRecord`. A scalar field
keeps its scalar column type; a nested record, list, dict, or data-carrying
union is stored as one JSON-in-TEXT column (`CBlob`), so a record's columns
stay flat and typed. Read a field codec's shape with `shape` and pass it here
when writing the `SRecord` list of a record codec.

    columnOf (shape Codec.int) == CInt
    columnOf (shape (Codec.list Codec.int)) == CBlob

## `toValue`

```ipe
toValue : Codec a -> a -> Value
```

The encoder half applied: `a` to a JSON `Value` node.

## `toJson`

```ipe
toJson : Codec a -> a -> String
```

Encode `a` to a compact JSON string.

## `fromJson`

```ipe
fromJson : Codec a -> String -> Result Error a
```

Decode a JSON string back to `a`, or a typed `Error` on malformed input or
a shape mismatch. Never panics: a bad document is an `Err`, not a crash. A
fresh decoder is built for this run, so a codec is safe to decode with
repeatedly.

## `fromJsonSafe`

```ipe
fromJsonSafe : Int -> Codec a -> String -> Result Error a
```

The untrusted-input door: reject input longer than `maxChars` BEFORE
decoding — a size guard for request bodies and webhooks — then decode. A
payload over the limit is a `LimitExceeded` error, never parsed. Parser
nesting depth is separately bounded by the JSON decoder itself, so this
guard plus the parser's depth bound cover both adversarial size and
adversarial nesting.

## `string`

```ipe
string : Codec String
```

JSON string ⇄ `String`. One `CText` column.

## `int`

```ipe
int : Codec Int
```

JSON integer ⇄ `Int`. A non-integral number is rejected, never truncated.
One `CInt` column.

## `bool`

```ipe
bool : Codec Bool
```

JSON boolean ⇄ `Bool`. One `CBool` column.

## `float`

```ipe
float : Codec Float
```

JSON number ⇄ `Float`. One `CReal` column. Prefer `decimal`/`money` for
exact quantities — a `Float` round-trip is lossy for prices.

## `decimal`

```ipe
decimal : Codec Decimal
```

Exact decimal ⇄ a JSON STRING, LOSSLESS. The value encodes through
`Decimal.toString` (its full precision) and decodes through
`Decimal.fromString`, so `12.345678901234567890` survives a round-trip a
`Float` would corrupt. One `CDecimal` column — TEXT affinity, but bound as
`SqlDecimal` so an exact quantity is never confused with a bare text field.

    -- Codec.fromJson Codec.decimal (Codec.toJson Codec.decimal d) == Ok d
    -- Codec.shape Codec.decimal == SScalar CDecimal

## `money`

```ipe
money : Codec Money
```

Exact money ⇄ a JSON STRING carrying both the amount and the ISO currency
code, LOSSLESS: `"12.34 USD"`. The amount encodes at full `Decimal` precision
(not rounded to the currency's minor units the way a formatted display would
round), and the currency survives verbatim, so the round-trip preserves the
exact stored quantity a `Float` cents field would corrupt. One `CMoney` column
— TEXT affinity, but bound as `SqlMoney` so a monetary value is never confused
with a bare text field or an exact decimal.

    -- Codec.fromJson Codec.money (Codec.toJson Codec.money m) == Ok m
    -- Codec.shape Codec.money == SScalar CMoney

## `timestamp`

```ipe
timestamp : Codec Timestamp
```

An instant ⇄ a JSON integer of Unix milliseconds. Encodes through
`Timestamp.toUnixMillis` and decodes through `Timestamp.fromUnixMillis`
(total: every `Int` is a valid instant), so the moment survives a round-trip
exactly. One `CTime` column — stored with INTEGER affinity, but bound as the
`SqlTime` role so a moment is never interchangeable with a plain count.

    -- Codec.fromJson Codec.timestamp (Codec.toJson Codec.timestamp t) == Ok t
    -- Codec.shape Codec.timestamp == SScalar CTime

## `map`

```ipe
map : (a -> b) -> (b -> a) -> Codec a -> Codec b
```

Adapt a `Codec a` to a `Codec b` given a BIJECTION `a <-> b`. Both
directions are required: `toB` reshapes a decoded `a` into a `b`, `toA`
reshapes a `b` back into an `a` the underlying encoder accepts. This is the
newtype-wrapper combinator (`UserId` over `String`); the inverse is what lets
the wrapped codec still encode. The wrapped codec keeps the inner codec's
`Shape` — a `UserId` newtype over `String` is still one `CText` column.

## `list`

```ipe
list : Codec a -> Codec (List a)
```

`list elem` — a JSON array of `elem`s ⇄ `List a`. The element encoder is
lifted over the array; the element decoder is lifted through the array
decoder, so a malformed element is a typed `Err`, never a partial list. A
list is one JSON-in-TEXT column (`SBlob`).

## `maybe`

```ipe
maybe : Codec a -> Codec (Maybe a)
```

`maybe elem` — JSON `null` ⇄ `Nothing`, any other value ⇄ `Just`. On
decode, only an explicit `null` becomes `Nothing`; a present-but-malformed
value is an `Err`, so a required field cannot be silently dropped. `Nothing`
encodes to `null`. A `maybe` over a scalar is a NULLABLE column of that scalar
(`CNull c`); a `maybe` over a blob shape stays a blob.

## `dict`

```ipe
dict : Codec a -> Codec (Dict String a)
```

`dict value` — a JSON object whose values are `value`s ⇄ `Dict String a`.
Keys are the object keys (strings); values run through the element codec. A
malformed value is a typed `Err`, never a partial dictionary. A dict is one
JSON-in-TEXT column (`SBlob`).

## `enum`

```ipe
enum : (a -> a -> Bool) -> List ( a, String ) -> Codec a
```

`enum eq pairs` — a nullary enum ⇄ a readable JSON string, driven by one
association list of `(constructor, wireName)` pairs that is the SINGLE source
of truth for both directions. `eq` is the constructor equality (a nullary
enum has no derived `==`, so it is supplied). Encode looks up the value's wire
name; decode reads a string and maps it back to the constructor. One `CText`
column — a queryable enum, not an opaque blob.

Fail-closed on both sides. On decode an unknown tag is a typed decode failure,
never a default constructor — the safe outcome is the only reachable one. On
encode a value absent from `pairs` (a caller that omitted a constructor)
encodes to `null`, which decode then rejects, so an incomplete map can never
silently round-trip a wrong constructor.

## `Variant`

One arm of a `taggedUnion`: it carries BOTH directions for one constructor,
so a variant list is a single source of truth — the encoder is derived from
the same list the decoder reads, never written separately. A `Variant a`
holds the wire tag, an encoder that (when the runtime value matches this arm)
yields the JSON payload node list, and a decoder that reads those payload
nodes back into the value.

## `taggedUnion`

```ipe
taggedUnion : List (Variant a) -> Codec a
```

`taggedUnion variants` — a data-carrying ADT ⇄ a tagged JSON array
`["Tag", arg0, arg1, …]`. Each `varN` supplies the projection that recognises
its arm; the decode side reads element 0 as the tag string and dispatches to
the matching variant's decoder. A data-carrying union is one JSON-in-TEXT
column (`SBlob`).

Fail-closed: a JSON tag with no matching variant is a typed decode failure,
never a default. The captured variant list is read (never consumed) per decode
run, so a codec is reusable.

## `var0`

```ipe
var0 : String -> a -> (a -> Bool) -> Variant a
```

A nullary variant: the tag alone, no payload. Encodes to `["Tag"]`.

## `var1`

```ipe
var1 : String -> (arg -> a) -> (a -> Maybe arg) -> Codec arg -> Variant a
```

A one-argument variant. `project` recognises this arm and yields its
argument for encode; `ctor` rebuilds the value from a decoded argument.

The inner codec's encoder is extracted to a plain `arg -> Value` binding
(`enc1`) OUTSIDE the `match` closure, so the closure CALLS the encoder rather
than forwarding a non-`Clone` codec value into it — the same
call-don't-forward shape the record encoder uses.

## `var2`

```ipe
var2 :
```

A two-argument variant.

## `var3`

```ipe
var3 :
```

A three-argument variant.
